title: Preparing for the Apollo Theatre, the supreme test
summary: After a week off to rehearse and get uniforms, the band faces the Apollo, which every Black act saw as the real test.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We finished I think it was a week at this club in Boston, and then we played that concert. After that, our next engagement was the Apollo Theatre in New York. I think we had about a week off when we got to New York, to rehearse, and we got new uniforms and the whole thing. By this time the band has got a good repertoire, and we're sounding pretty tight, and the whole thing is just about like we wanted it to be.

Of course, at that particular time, the Apollo Theatre was the supreme test for any band or any act or whatever, because no matter where in the country you'd been... And we had had a successful tour, because Billy Eckstine was very hot during that time from the Earl Hines days. So our dances were

pretty well attended, you know. But the Apollo Theatre was still the test, no matter where you'd been and what you'd done. As a matter of New York was, is, has been and always will be, I guess, the real test for any artist. But at that particular time, the Black bands or acts or whatever, if you made it in the Apollo Theatre, then you figured you had it going.
